question: Should OpenClaw adopt this global operational-reply policy, and should redirect persistence failures remain fail-closed rather than retrying or falling back to the source chat?
rationale: The policy adds a public configuration surface and durable delivery behavior across core runtime paths; choosing between confidentiality, operator visibility, and retry semantics is a product and security contract, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor fail-closed policy
options.body: Approve a generic core policy with `always` as the compatible default and retain source suppression when the operator-session write fails, pending focused real-channel proof.

options.title: Require retry semantics
options.body: Define a bounded, observable retry contract for operator-session persistence before accepting redirect mode, without falling back to the source chat.

options.title: Defer the global surface
options.body: Keep existing delivery behavior until maintainers want to own the config, state, and cross-channel policy contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Approve a generic core policy with `always` as the compatible default and retain source suppression when the operator-session write fails, pending focused real-channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked implementation discussion identifies a maintainer/security-owner decision on the redirect-failure contract.
